narrative: The market is currently in a risk-off state following the sudden ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid misconduct and espionage allegations. This leadership crisis has triggered significant volatility in the semiconductor sector and broader equity indices, compounded by ongoing Justice Department probes. While AI infrastructure demand remains robust as evidenced by strong earnings from Applied Materials and Cisco, investors are rotating capital and reassessing valuations. Geopolitical tensions between the US and China over chip export controls are intensifying, adding a layer of regulatory uncertainty. Meanwhile, crude oil is rallying on supply concerns and geopolitical developments, while gold has faced downward pressure.

Nasdaq.why: The index is under significant pressure from the Nvidia sell-off, though anchors note it remains supported by other tech components and strong earnings from peers like Cisco and Applied Materials.

S&P 500.why: The index is showing resilience as gains in non-AI sectors partially offset the losses caused by the leadership crisis at Nvidia.

Gold.why: Spot gold has seen a decline of approximately 2.7%, trading down to $3,882 per ounce.

Oil.why: Crude oil is rallying, with WTI up 2.8% and Brent up 3.5%, driven by geopolitical developments and supply concerns.

priced_in: Increased volatility for the semiconductor and AI sectors
Heightened regulatory and legislative risk for technology companies

debates: Whether the AI infrastructure build-out remains a long-term growth story despite the leadership crisis at its primary driver, Nvidia
